words.definition: Showing great care and steady, constant effort over a long period of time.
words.example: The assiduous intern arrived early each day and double-checked every figure before the meeting.
words.mnemonic: From Latin 'assidēre,' to sit down to — picture someone always sitting at the desk, working: 'a-SIT-uous.'

words.definition: Unwilling to work or exert energy; habitually inactive and idle.
words.example: So slothful was he that the lawn went uncut for the entire summer.
words.mnemonic: Think of the sloth, the animal so slow it barely stirs from its branch.

words.definition: Feeling drowsy, sluggish, and drained of energy or enthusiasm.
words.example: After the heavy lunch, the whole office grew lethargic and struggled to focus.
words.mnemonic: 'Leth' echoes Lethe, the mythical river whose waters made souls forget and grow drowsy.

words.definition: Continuing without pause or mercy; refusing to ease off or give up.
words.example: The relentless rain battered the coast for three days without a single break.
words.mnemonic: Someone who never 'relents' — 'relent-less' means less letting up, ever.

words.definition: To have a strong desire to reach a high goal or achievement.
words.example: She aspired to become the first doctor in her family.
words.mnemonic: Hear 'a spire' — you reach upward toward a tall church spire, aiming high.

words.definition: A strong hope or ambition to accomplish a significant goal.
words.example: Her lifelong aspiration was to sail solo around the world.
words.mnemonic: Contains 'a spire' — a hope pointed high, like a spire reaching toward the sky.

words.definition: Having a strong drive to succeed, gain power, or reach high goals.
words.example: The ambitious young lawyer set her sights on becoming a partner within five years.
words.mnemonic: Hides 'bit' — but such a person never wants just a little bit; they want it all.

words.definition: Ready to start new ventures and full of resourceful, energetic ideas.
words.example: The enterprising teenager built a lawn-mowing business across three neighborhoods.
words.mnemonic: Contains 'enterprise' — the trait of someone eager to launch a bold new business.

words.definition: The power or willingness to begin and pursue action on one's own.
words.example: Without being asked, she took the initiative and reorganized the entire filing system.
words.mnemonic: Begins with 'init,' like 'initial' — being the first to start something.

words.definition: A career or occupation that someone feels strongly called to pursue.
words.example: Teaching was less a job than a vocation for her, a true calling.
words.mnemonic: Shares a root with 'voice' (Latin 'vocare,' to call) — a calling that calls to you.

words.definition: Long, hard, and tiring physical or mental work.
words.example: After a day of toil in the fields, the farmers slept deeply.
words.mnemonic: Rhymes with 'boil' — you sweat and boil from exhausting labor.

words.definition: The use of much physical or mental energy to accomplish something.
words.example: Climbing the steep trail took such exertion that his legs trembled at the top.
words.mnemonic: Contains 'exert' — you exert force, pushing hard with all your energy.

words.definition: To make a serious and determined attempt to achieve something.
words.example: The team endeavored to finish the bridge before the winter storms arrived.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'end' + 'favor' — you push hard so things end in your favor.

words.definition: To make great efforts to achieve or obtain something difficult.
words.example: Even after three failed attempts, she continued to strive for a perfect score on the exam.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'drive' — you strive when you have the inner drive to push hard toward a goal.

words.definition: To keep trying and not give up despite obstacles or discouragement.
words.example: Though the experiment failed twenty times, she persevered until it finally worked.
words.mnemonic: 'Per' (through) + 'severe' — push through severe hardship without quitting.

words.definition: The steady refusal to give up on a goal despite difficulty, failure, or delay.
words.example: Her perseverance carried her through four failed attempts before the experiment finally worked.
words.mnemonic: Break it up: 'persevere' hides 'severe' — you keep going even when things get severe.

words.definition: The rate at which useful work or output gets done in a given amount of time.
words.example: After switching off notifications, his productivity jumped and he cleared the whole backlog by noon.
words.mnemonic: Root 'produce' + '-tivity' — how much stuff you can produce in an hour.

words.definition: Achieving a result with little wasted effort, time, or resources.
words.example: The new engine is so efficient that it travels twice as far on the same tank of fuel.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'a fish went' — a fish glides through water wasting no motion.

words.definition: Having the skill and knowledge needed to do something to an acceptable standard.
words.example: You want a competent electrician for this job, not someone guessing at the wiring.
words.mnemonic: 'Compete' + 'ent' — you're skilled enough to actually compete for the job.

words.definition: Highly skilled at a particular activity through practice or natural talent.
words.example: She is remarkably adept at defusing arguments before they turn into shouting matches.
words.mnemonic: 'A' + 'dept' — go to any department and this person is the expert there.

words.definition: Well practiced and reliably good at a skill, though not necessarily a master.
words.example: Two years of lessons left him proficient enough to hold a conversation in Japanese.
words.mnemonic: 'Pro' + 'efficient' — a pro who does the task efficiently every time.

words.definition: Deep specialized knowledge or skill gained from long experience in a field.
words.example: When the bridge cracked, the city called in an engineer whose expertise was structural failure.
words.mnemonic: 'Expert' + '-ise' — literally the state of being an expert.

words.definition: Complete command of a subject or skill, at the highest level of ability.
words.example: His mastery of the violin was obvious the moment his bow touched the strings.
words.mnemonic: A 'master' craftsman has it — '-y' turns master into the thing they possess.

words.definition: Highly skilled and successful, having reached an impressive level in some pursuit.
words.example: By thirty she was an accomplished pianist who had toured three continents.
words.mnemonic: Contains 'accomplish' — you've clearly accomplished a lot to earn the label.

words.definition: Careful to do tasks correctly and to fulfill duties honestly and responsibly.
words.example: A conscientious nurse, she double-checked every dosage before it reached a patient.
words.mnemonic: Hear 'conscience' inside it — your conscience nags you to do the job right.

words.definition: Done with great care and attention to every small detail.
words.example: Restoring the old painting was painstaking work, one square inch cleaned at a time.
words.mnemonic: 'Pains' + 'taking' — you take pains, going to great trouble over details.

words.definition: Complete and careful, leaving out no detail or part of the task.
words.example: The detective gave the room such a thorough search that even the floorboards came up.
words.mnemonic: It goes 'through' everything — spelled like 'through' with an extra 'o'.

words.definition: Demanding great care, effort, or precision; hard to satisfy.
words.example: The watchmaker held her apprentices to exacting standards, rejecting any gear a hair off size.
words.mnemonic: From 'exact' — it demands you be exact, down to the tiniest measurement.

words.definition: Clever at finding quick, practical ways to solve problems with what is available.
words.example: Stranded with a flat tire and no jack, the resourceful driver used a log and a boulder.
words.mnemonic: 'Resource' + 'full' — full of resources, always finding a way out.

words.definition: Deeply loyal and committed to a person, cause, or activity.
words.example: A devoted fan, he has attended every home game for the past twenty seasons.
words.mnemonic: From 'vow' — someone devoted has taken a vow and sticks to it.

words.definition: Committed and hardworking, giving much time and energy to a cause or purpose.
words.example: The dedicated nurse stayed hours past her shift to comfort frightened patients.
words.mnemonic: From Latin 'dicare', to devote — picture solemnly devoting a monument, pouring all your effort into it.

words.definition: Done as a routine duty, without real interest, care, or effort.
words.example: He gave the report a perfunctory glance and signed it without reading a word.
words.mnemonic: 'Perform' + 'functory' → just going through the functions and motions, nothing more.

words.definition: Hasty and shallow, not paying attention to detail.
words.example: A cursory glance at the contract missed the clause that later cost her thousands.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'cursor' — your mouse cursor zips quickly across the screen, only skimming the surface.

words.definition: Failing to give proper care or attention to something one is responsible for.
words.example: The negligent landlord ignored the broken smoke alarm for months.
words.mnemonic: Hidden inside is 'neglect' — to neglect is to leave undone what you should do.

words.definition: Careless about a duty; failing to do what should be done.
words.example: I would be remiss if I didn't thank the volunteers who made tonight possible.
words.mnemonic: 'Re-MISS' — you keep missing your responsibilities again and again.

words.definition: Not working or being used; spending time doing nothing.
words.example: With the factory closed, the machines sat idle and the workers waited for news.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'idol' — a statue idol just stands there, unmoving and unused.

words.definition: Lacking energy, enthusiasm, or the will to do anything.
words.example: Feverish and listless, the child pushed away even her favorite toys.
words.mnemonic: 'List-less' — no list of things you feel like doing; no desire, no spark.

words.definition: Moving slowly and with little energy; pleasantly relaxed or drooping.
words.example: The languid afternoon heat left everyone sprawled in hammocks, too drowsy to move.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'languish' and 'lag' — you lag and droop, slow and heavy.

words.definition: To keep putting off something that should be done now.
words.example: She procrastinated all week and ended up writing the essay at 3 a.m.
words.mnemonic: Contains Latin 'cras', meaning tomorrow — always saying 'I'll do it tomorrow.'

words.definition: To waste time or move so slowly that a task takes far too long.
words.example: Stop dawdling over your cereal or you'll miss the school bus!
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'doodle' — instead of working you doodle and drift, letting time slip by.

words.definition: To avoid or neglect a duty, responsibility, or task.
words.example: He shirked the dishes every night, leaving them piled up for his roommate.
words.mnemonic: Rhymes with 'work' — but a shirker shrinks from work instead of doing it.

words.definition: To waste money, time, or resources in a careless, foolish way.
words.example: He squandered his inheritance on fast cars and lost bets within a single year.
words.mnemonic: Ends like 'wander' — let your cash wander off aimlessly until it's gone.

words.definition: To waste time or money little by little on unimportant things.
words.example: She frittered away the whole morning scrolling aimlessly through her phone.
words.mnemonic: Picture a fried fritter crumbling into little bits — just as you waste time bit by bit.

words.definition: To struggle clumsily or helplessly, unsure of what to do next.
words.example: New to the language, he floundered through the interview, grasping for words.
words.mnemonic: A flounder is a flatfish — picture it flopping helplessly on the deck, struggling to move.

words.definition: To hesitate, stumble, or lose strength and confidence in action or speech.
words.example: Her voice faltered as she read the last letter her mother had written.
words.mnemonic: 'Fault' + 'alter' — a fault makes your steps alter and waver, almost falling.

words.definition: To grow strong, wealthy, or successful over a period of time.
words.example: After years of hard work, the small bakery began to prosper and opened three new locations.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'prosperity' — picture a 'pro' who 'spurs' growth until money piles up.

words.definition: To perform far better than others or above the usual standard.
words.example: She always excelled in mathematics, solving problems her classmates found impossible.
words.mnemonic: Hidden inside 'excellent' — to do this is to be excellent at the task.

words.definition: To be greater than, or go beyond, a limit, rival, or expectation.
words.example: The new phone's sales surpassed every forecast the company had made.
words.mnemonic: 'Sur-' means over (as in surplus) plus 'pass' — to pass right over and beyond.

words.definition: To leave behind or exceed by moving faster or growing greater.
words.example: Demand for the vaccine quickly outstripped the available supply.
words.mnemonic: 'Out' + 'strip' — imagine running so fast you strip past everyone on the track.

words.definition: To make something seem far less important by being much more impressive.
words.example: Her groundbreaking discovery eclipsed all the work done before her.
words.mnemonic: Like a solar eclipse, the moon blots out the sun — one thing overshadows another.

words.definition: To reach or gain something through sustained effort.
words.example: After months of training, he finally attained his black belt in judo.
words.mnemonic: 'A-tain' sounds like 'a train' pulling into its station — you arrive at your goal.

words.definition: To carry out, complete, or satisfy a duty, promise, or need.
words.example: The company fulfilled its promise to plant a tree for every order placed.
words.mnemonic: 'Full' + 'fill' — you fill the obligation completely full, satisfying it.

words.definition: To complete or bring to a perfect, final finish.
words.example: They consummated the merger with a handshake and a signed contract.
words.mnemonic: 'Con-' + 'summate' (sum) — you sum everything up and seal the deal.

words.definition: To gather or collect something, especially support, praise, or information.
words.example: The film garnered widespread acclaim at the festival.
words.mnemonic: Echoes 'granary' — a barn where you gather and store the harvested grain.

words.definition: To gather together a large quantity of something over time.
words.example: Over decades, the collector amassed thousands of rare stamps.
words.mnemonic: 'A' + 'mass' — you build up a huge mass of stuff into one heap.

words.definition: Requiring great effort and hard to endure.
words.example: The arduous climb up the mountain left the hikers utterly exhausted.
words.mnemonic: 'Ard' rhymes with 'hard' — an arduous job is punishingly hard.

words.definition: Needing a lot of time and painstaking effort to complete.
words.example: Copying the entire manuscript by hand was a laborious process that took months.
words.mnemonic: Contains 'labor' — this kind of work demands heavy, sweaty labor.

words.definition: Working with great energy for a long time without becoming weary.
words.example: The nurse was tireless, taking double shifts throughout the whole crisis.
words.mnemonic: 'Tire' + 'less' — someone with less capacity to grow weary, always going.

words.definition: A natural talent or capacity to learn or do something well.
words.example: Her aptitude for languages let her pick up Spanish in just a few weeks.
words.mnemonic: 'Apt' means suited or capable — this is a fittingly natural skill.

words.definition: To obtain something, especially with care, effort, or cunning.
words.example: The chef procured fresh truffles from a specialist supplier in Italy.
words.mnemonic: 'Pro-' + 'cure' — a doctor gets hold of the cure by obtaining the right medicine.

words.definition: The quality of holding firmly to a goal despite difficulty or opposition.
words.example: Her tenacity kept her training through two injuries until she finally made the Olympic team.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'ten-acity' — picture gripping a rope with all ten fingers and refusing to let go.
